entry_points.call: import interior_kit as k; k.reset_tags(); v, t = k.corridor_section(21.6, doors=((9.0, 1), (21.0, 0))); spans = k.tagged_spans(t); k.write_obj(path, v, t, spans)   # 5,344 v / 7,656 t -> g structure, light_portal_head, light_downlight, light_pilaster_strip. THE `spans` ARGUMENT IS NOT OPTIONAL: write_obj(path, v, t) with no spans emits ONE group, 'structure', and the light fittings vanish.

import interior_kit as k; k.reset_tags(); v, t = k.corridor_junction_section(7.2, arms=(0, 1, 2, 3)); spans = k.tagged_spans(t); k.write_obj(path, v, t, spans)   # 7,032 v / 10,644 t. arms=(0,1,3) gives a tee, 5,578 v / 8,444 t. Same 4 groups either way.

import interior_kit as k; k.reset_tags(); v, t = k.bulkhead(k.chamfered_arch(2.6, 3.0, 0.5)); spans = k.tagged_spans(t)   # 80 v / 52 t, spans == []. `section` is a POLYGON, not a string -- bulkhead('full') raises IndexError inside _signed_area because it indexes the string's characters.
import interior_kit as k; k.reset_tags(); v, t = k.deck_grid(21.6, 2.6); spans = k.tagged_spans(t)   # 1,120 v / 1,680 t, spans == [] -> everything is 'structure'.

# The full sweep I actually ran, all 19 public builders: ring_frame(3.0,0.35,0.28,segments=16), deck_panel(2.6,1.5), handrail(4.0), wall_panel(1.3,2.0), rib_arch(9.0,7.2), downlight_pool(), deck_strip(0.9,10.0), chamfered_arch/aperture, portal_frame(2.6,3.0), pilaster(2.5), wall_assembly(3.05,3.0), door_frame(), door_leaf(open_fraction=0.35), door_assembly(section=k.chamfered_arch(2.6,3.0,0.5)), bulkhead(...), deck_grid(...), junction((0,1,2,3)), corridor_section(...), corridor_junction_section(...). Union of every group any of them emits = exactly 4.
import signage; signage.write_obj(path)   # -> board_pair(); 168 v / 144 t; g sign_post, sign_frame, sign_face (24 / 96 / 24 tris)

import signage; verts, tris, groups = signage.board_pair()   # in-memory. NOTE: `groups` is a PER-TRIANGLE list of names (len == len(tris)), NOT (name, lo, hi) spans -- a different contract from interior_kit.tagged_spans(). signage.board(with_post=False) drops sign_post and emits only 2 groups.

materials.name: sign_mount_dark
materials.title: Sign Mount — dark structural post and board frame, matte painted steel
materials.source: reference/01-station-exterior/welcome to babylon 5.webp (authority 1, 1000x750; reference/00-INDEX.md files it as 'misfiled — this is signage, not exterior' and calls it 'two backlit blue information boards in the customs hall'). MEASURED RAW, NOT BALANCED — see extrapolated. POST, clear of both boards, (0.610,0.400)-(0.675,0.600): median rgb(0.094, 0.082, 0.094), S 0.125, luminance 0.086, max luminance 0.109 over 9,750 px, p99 0.098. POST over its full visible height (0.595,0.150)-(0.690,0.950): median rgb(0.098, 0.090, 0.102), S 0.115, luminance 0.094, n = 57,000, B−R +0.004, R−G +0.008; the three bands (0.600,0.13)-(0.685,0.30), (0.600,0.38)-(0.685,0.62), (0.600,0.72)-(0.685,0.95) read luminance 0.082 / 0.086 / 0.114. THE LEFT BOARD'S OWN FRAME FACE, a different object, (0.566,0.300)-(0.596,0.470): median rgb(0.090, 0.078, 0.090), luminance 0.082 — identical to the post to within 0.004 in every channel, which is why frame and post are one material and not two. A horizontal profile at y 250-270 across x 566-598 is flat to ±0.003 in every channel over 32 px. THE BRIGHT RIM at the panel edge, (0.558,0.280)-(0.566,0.345), median rgb(0.141, 0.137, 0.184), peak rgb(0.199, 0.195, 0.223) at x=562 — see reasoning, it is light and not paint. SAME-FRAME CONTROL, the ceiling structure lit only by the dim ambient: (0.30,0.005)-(0.50,0.05) median rgb(0.055, 0.035, 0.055), R/G 1.57, and (0.70,0.005)-(0.90,0.06) rgb(0.075, 0.047, 0.059), R/G 1.60. LEVEL anchored to station/materials.py's sign_neon_venue board ground (0.094, 0.100, 0.112), luminance 0.0996, measured off reference/11-props-and-technology/Zocalo neon signage in background.jpg in a different frame, different sector and different session.
materials.extrapolated: THE LEVEL, and the decision to measure this frame raw. Both are declared in full. (1) GREY-WORLD FAILS ON THIS FRAME, and I checked rather than assumed. Its gains are (1.262, 1.276, 0.702), and its balanced mid-tone population (0.15 < V < 0.85) has median saturation 0.299 and p90 0.469 against the anchor frame grey level 1.webp's 0.105 / 0.194 computed identically. More than half the frame is a saturated blue lightbox, so grey-world fits the lightbox rather than the illuminant. This is the Doug's Dugout failure NEGATIVE_RESULTS already records (0.370 / 0.870, a third of pixels above S 0.5), one notch milder — this frame is 0.046 above S 0.5. The library already treats this frame as measure-raw without saying so: signage_panel quotes raw rgb(0.151, 0.156, 0.434). My method reproduces GREY_WORLD_GAINS for grey level 1.webp (0.970/1.087/0.953) and dock.webp (0.968/1.027/1.006) to three decimals, so the failure is the frame's and not the method's. RECOMMEND ADDING TO NEGATIVE_RESULTS so nobody balances it. (2) THE HUE IS MEASURED, not extrapolated: neutral. (3) THE LEVEL IS EXTRAPOLATED. The post is lit only by a dim off-frame ambient and this frame holds no reflectance reference, so a raw luminance of 0.086 is radiance and not albedo. 0.1006 comes from sign_neon_venue's measured 0.0996 — the library's one measured value for the same object class, the dark ground a lit sign board is built on — and the two agree to 1%. It is 0.219 x ALBEDO_ANCHOR, i.e. a charcoal grey, which is a real paint value (0.08-0.12 sRGB) rather than a number picked to look right. The 3% warm bias (R/G 1.030) is half the 6% hull_exterior declares as invented and is kept for the same reason: the only ambient this object ever sees in the reference is warm. OVERTURNED BY: any customs-hall or concourse frame that shows a sign post under a measurable neutral key; if one appears, the level is measurable and this stops being an extrapolation. A frame that separates the board bezel from the post — the bezel painted lighter, say — splits this into two materials, and the split is one edit because the two binds are already listed separately.
materials.reasoning: WHAT THESE TWO GROUPS ARE. signage.py builds the customs boards as three pieces: sign_post, 'the dark structural post the boards hang on', 0.34 m wide and running from the deck to 0.22 m above the board top; sign_frame, four rails 0.075 m wide and 0.11 m deep forming the bezel; and sign_face, the lit panel recessed 0.035 m inside them. This material is the first two. ONE MATERIAL, NOT TWO, AND THE FRAME SAYS SO. The board's own frame face and the post 30 px away measure rgb(0.090, 0.078, 0.090) and rgb(0.094, 0.082, 0.094) — identical to within 0.004 in every channel. That is as strong an in-frame identity as this reference set ever offers, and the library's own doctrine (sign_deck_plaque, and the 'two reds, measured separately' note on accent_warning) is to split a register only where a frame splits it. Here nothing splits it. NEUTRAL, AND THIS IS THE PROJECT'S STANDING TEST PASSING IN ITS STRONG FORM. The post stands beside two large panels whose field is B−R +0.282. A neutral surface receiving significant light from them would go blue; the post reads B−R +0.004 over 57,000 px, so the panels contribute almost nothing to it and its illuminant is the dim warm ambient. Under that ambient the ceiling structure reads R/G 1.57-1.60 while the post reads R/G 1.15 — same light, two surfaces, two different warmths, so the warmth follows the object and not the light. The post is therefore a neutral surface under a warm ambient, and painting it warm would be the ochre-dado mistake NEGATIVE_RESULTS records five times over. Its raw saturation of 0.115-0.125 is already below STRUCTURAL_SAT_MAX before any correction. MATTE, AND THAT IS MEASURED. Over 9,750 px of post standing within a metre of two roughly 1.4 m^2 lightboxes, max luminance is 0.109 against a median of 0.086 — a 1.27x max-to-median, p99 only 1.14x. A glossy dark column beside a source that size would show it reflected; nothing resolves. Roughness 0.70 places it just under sign_deck_plaque's 0.72 (matte painted sign hardware, same family) and at shell_wall_industrial's 0.70, and well above door_leaf_painted's 0.42, because a structural post is a harder finish than a plaque but is not a door leaf. Specular 0.35 matches sign_deck_plaque and kit_wall_plate, and is low because the frame returns no specular. METALLIC 0.0: a painted enclosure is a dielectric with the steel under the coat, which is exactly the distinction plant_switchgear documents when it explains why it sits at 0.0 while hull_exterior sits at 0.34 for 48 m of plating worn through in places. A 0.34 m post has no such story. TEXTURE NULL, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OMISSION. The frame face is flat to ±0.003 over 32 px and the post's p99/median is 1.14 — no plate seam, stud or weld run resolves anywhere on it. The object is also small: the frame rails are 75 mm wide, and wall_plate at its 4.0 m repeat would lay 1/53 of a plate across a rail, which is plant_valve_metal's documented reason for going untextured. THE BRIGHT RIM NEEDS NO MATERIAL OF ITS OWN, and this is the argument for why. A 2-3 px pale line runs the whole perimeter of each board between the blue field and the dark surround, peaking at rgb(0.199, 0.195, 0.223) — near-neutral, five to seven stops of the surrounding hardware. It is the inner arris of the frame rails catching the recessed face's own backlight, which is precisely what signage.py built the recess to produce ('the frame casts a shadow onto the face, and a decal cannot'). In the engine those inner rail faces are already modelled and will be lit by the emissive face; giving them a brighter albedo would paint in a lighting effect and would double it.

materials.name: signage_panel
materials.title: Signage Panel — backlit blue with neutral lettering
materials.source: reference/01-station-exterior/welcome to babylon 5.webp (authority 1). This is the EXISTING material's own source, unchanged, and signage.py's board is literally the object it was measured from. INDEPENDENT RE-MEASUREMENT, this session, over the panel region (0.020,0.320)-(0.520,0.950), n = 236,000: median rgb(0.227, 0.227, 0.510), B−R = +0.282, R−G = 0.000. materials.py PROVENANCE's four clusters over the same panel give B−R = 0.283 / 0.282 / 0.282 / 0.278 — one constant blue emission with neutral lettering added on top, reproduced to 0.001 from a different statistic (region median vs k-means). The right-hand board, a second panel in the same frame, (0.75,0.62)-(0.95,0.72): median rgb(0.271, 0.275, 0.514), B−R +0.243, R−G −0.004. The panel darkens toward its rim — a profile at y 250-270 runs luminance 0.074 at x=548 down to 0.055 at x=556 before the frame edge — which is the recessed face falling into its own bezel shadow.
materials.extrapolated: NOTHING NEW. Every value here is station/materials.py's existing signage_panel, unchanged, re-stated so the record is complete. Its own declared extrapolations stand.
materials.reasoning: THIS IS A BIND ADDITION, NOT A NEW MATERIAL. Apply it by hand as one token: signage_panel.binds becomes ('signage_panel', 'sign_face'). Do NOT emit a Material(...) block for it — station/apply_proposals.py::validate will reject a name already in BY_NAME whose binds differ, and that rejection is correct. WHY REUSE RATHER THAN DUPLICATE. signage_panel was measured off the very boards signage.py builds, in the same frame, and my independent re-measurement reproduces its B−R signature to 0.001. A second material for the same object would be two sources of truth for one surface. Fragment safety checked by running it: 'sign_face' matches nothing in the 278-group universe (rooms.py's 124, command_control, council_chamber, docking_bay, signage, interior_kit and materials.KNOWN_GROUPS) except itself, no existing bind is a substring of it, and adding it creates no ambiguity — test_materials_layer3.ambiguous(['sign_face']) is empty. TWO THINGS THE NEXT AGENT MUST FIX IN signage.py, NOT IN materials.py. (1) NO UVs. signage_panel is the library's one triplanar=False material and its own note says 'whatever mesh carries this group must ship UVs'. signage._M.box computes none and interior.write_grouped_obj writes no vt lines at all, so the group would sample an unmapped mesh. (2) A DOUBLED BEZEL. materials.gen_signage_sheet paints its own bezel into the sheet — a 4.5%-per-side border at rgb(0.120, 0.122, 0.130), which is incidentally a near-neutral dark that corroborates sign_mount_dark's reading of the real hardware — while signage.py models the bezel as separate sign_frame rails. Applied naively the board gets two frames, one modelled and one painted. The fix is to map sign_face's UVs to the sheet's interior, inset past the bezel, and it belongs with the UV work.

findings:
"1. interior_kit EMITS FOUR GROUPS, NOT FOURTEEN, AND materials.KNOWN_GROUPS IS WRONG ABOUT TEN OF THEM. Running all 19 public builders, the union of every group any code path produces is exactly {structure, light_downlight, light_pilaster_strip, light_portal_head}. materials.KNOWN_GROUPS lists fourteen interior-kit groups; the other ten -- wall_panel, wall_assembly, pilaster, portal_frame, door_frame, door_leaf, bulkhead, deck_grid, deck_panel, light_deck_channel -- are never emitted by anything. kit_pilaster, kit_rail_band, kit_reveal, kit_skirt, kit_deck and kit_deck_plate are therefore bound to fragments that no mesh in this project carries. They are not wrong materials; they are materials with nothing to attach to.

2. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR LAYER 3: THE ENTIRE CORRIDOR IS ONE MATERIAL. 6,264 of corridor_section's 7,656 triangles (82%) are untagged and land in 'structure', which kit_wall_plate claims. Deck, soffit, portal frames, pilasters, doors, skirt and wall plates all render as the same 0.46 grey. The gate's rule 5 -- a deck must be darker AND smoother than the wall it meets -- cannot even be evaluated on the kit, because there is no deck group. So the kit will pass a coverage check while failing the layer's actual intent. THE FIX IS IN interior_kit.py, NOT IN materials.py: wrap the existing builders in `with tag(...)` blocks named for the fragments materials.py already declares. Every material needed is already written and measured. Do not add materials for this; add tags.

3. light_deck_channel IS DEAD CODE, AND THE BUG IS ONE LINE. deck_panel() opens `with tag('light_deck_channel')` and then calls the bare `_box` imported from components. Tagging only records through the `_tagging` decorator (which wraps _slab, _prism and _plate_with_hole) and through `_merge`; `_box` goes through neither, and the `tag` context manager itself records nothing on exit. So the corridor's continuous floor light strip -- the single feature the module's own docstring calls 'the single continuous floor light central corridor.webp shows' -- emits zero tagged triangles and falls into 'structure'. The light_deck_channel material exists, resolves, and is never reached. Fix: use `_slab` inside that block, or decorate the call.

4. THE COMMITTED KIT OBJs HAVE NO LIGHTS IN THEM, AND THIS IS A REGRESSION OF A DOCUMENTED BUG. station/generated/interior_corridor.obj and interior_junction.obj each contain exactly one group, 'g structure'. interior_kit's __main__ calls write_obj(path, v, t) without the `spans` argument, so the light fittings are merged into the default group and disappear. write_obj's own docstring says what that costs: 'without it the whole kit rendered as a dark tube and its lighting premise went untested for two sessions'. The spans parameter was added; the caller was never updated. Any render made from those committed files has been judging a corridor with no light fittings.

5. light_pilaster_strip IS AMBIGUOUS AND ONLY RESOLVES CORRECTLY BY ACCIDENT OF NAME LENGTH. Both kit_pilaster (fragment 'pilaster') and light_pilaster_strip (fragment 'light_pilaster_strip') match the group. Longest-wins gives the right answer today, 19 characters against 8. test_materials_layer3.ambiguous() classifies exactly this shape as a defect -- it is the '_wall vs prop_monitor_wall' case its docstring names -- and it fires on this pair. It is currently invisible because interior_kit has no BESPOKE_BUILDERS entry, so the gate never sees the group. Adding the entry point below will make the gate report it.

6. THE SIGNAGE FRAME CANNOT BE GREY-WORLD BALANCED, AND NOTHING SAYS SO. 'welcome to babylon 5.webp' gives gains (1.262, 1.276, 0.702) and a balanced mid-tone saturation of median 0.299 / p90 0.469 against the anchor frame's 0.105 / 0.194 -- the Doug's Dugout failure mode, milder. The frame is more than half a saturated blue lightbox, so grey-world fits the lightbox. materials.py already measures it raw (signage_panel quotes raw values) but never records why. This belongs in NEGATIVE_RESULTS beside the Dugout entry: it is the second frame in the set that must not be balanced, and for the same structural reason -- the mid-tone population is not neutral.

7. METHOD CONTROL. My grey-world implementation reproduces GREY_WORLD_GAINS for grey level 1.webp as (0.970, 1.087, 0.953) and dock.webp as (0.968, 1.027, 1.006) -- both exact to three decimals -- so the balance failures above are properties of the frames and not of my measurement. Every number I report was computed this session from the pixels, not recalled.

8. bulkhead(section) TAKES A POLYGON. A previous pass that tried bulkhead('full') would have hit IndexError: string index out of range inside _signed_area, which indexes the string's characters as if they were (x, y) pairs. The working call is k.bulkhead(k.chamfered_arch(2.6, 3.0, 0.5)). Reported because it looks like a module that 'raises' and is not."
coverage_note:
"BOTH MODULES FULLY ENUMERATED BY RUNNING THEM. Nothing here was grepped; every group name came out of a returned tris list or an OBJ written to disk. 7 groups total: 4 from interior_kit, 3 from signage. The partial pass's figures for the other four modules are consistent with my method -- signage reproduces at exactly 3 (sign_post, sign_frame, sign_face).

interior_kit: 4 / 4 ALREADY RESOLVE. No proposal is needed and none is made. Verified by calling materials.resolve(group, 'interior') on each:
  structure            -> kit_wall_plate       (fragment 'structure')
  light_downlight      -> light_downlight
  light_pilaster_strip -> light_pilaster_strip (ambiguous with kit_pilaster; longest-wins picks correctly -- see finding 5)
  light_portal_head    -> light_portal_head
test_materials_layer3.unresolved([...]) returns [] for the set. The kit's layer-3 problem is not missing materials, it is missing tags -- see findings 1-4. Ten of the fourteen interior-kit entries in materials.KNOWN_GROUPS are emitted by nothing, and six kit_* materials are consequently unreachable.

signage: 0 / 3 resolved before this proposal, 3 / 3 after. sign_frame and sign_post take one new material, sign_mount_dark, because the frame shows them as one surface to within 0.004 in every channel. sign_face takes a BIND ADDITION to the existing signage_panel -- it is literally the object signage_panel was measured from -- and must be applied by hand as one token rather than through apply_proposals.py, which will correctly refuse a duplicate name.

FRAGMENT SAFETY, CHECKED BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY EYE. I built the full group universe -- rooms.py's 124 procedural groups, command_control's, council_chamber's, docking_bay's, signage's, interior_kit's 4, plus all of materials.KNOWN_GROUPS, 278 names -- and tested each new fragment against every one of them and against all 221 existing binds. 'sign_face', 'sign_frame' and 'sign_post' each match exactly one group (their own), no existing bind is a substring of any of them, and no existing material claims any of them. test_materials_layer3.ambiguous() on the three returns [].

GATE PRE-CHECK. sign_mount_dark: saturation 0.039 (ceiling 0.20), luminance 0.1006 (0.219 x ALBEDO_ANCHOR), roughness 0.70 (mirror floor 0.15), metallic 0.0, specular 0.35, all in [0, 1]; source cites 'welcome to babylon 5.webp' and 'Zocalo neon signage in background.jpg', both of which exist in the repo, neither quarantined; texture null so no uv_scale_denom is required. Neither material is a deck or a wall, so the deck/wall pairing rule does not apply. No 21-QUARANTINE or 22-QUARANTINE frame was opened.

NOT COVERED, AND SAID PLAINLY: I did not build interior_kit through test_materials_layer3.BESPOKE_BUILDERS because it has no write_obj(path) signature -- its write_obj takes (path, verts, tris, spans). The next agent should add an entry that calls corridor_junction_section and passes tagged_spans, which is the widest single piece and produces all four groups; the exact call is in entry_points. Once it is in, the gate will see the light_pilaster_strip ambiguity that is currently invisible to it."
